Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
221 PM EDT Thu Aug 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 220 PM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes we made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 220 PM EDT Thursday...

1. Isolated to scattered showers and an isolated thunderstorm 
or two is expected this afternoon. Conditions turn drier and quieter 
by Friday and Saturday.

2. Seasonable temperatures next week and a couple shower 
chances.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 220 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Another shortwave is expected to move through this 
afternoon, and is currently centered over the St. Lawrence River. As 
opposed to yesterdays forecast, trends have decreased for any wider 
shower and thunderstorm coverage through this afternoon. Subsidence 
in the wake of convection from last night and seasonably cool 
temperatures in the low to mid 70s has capped much of the region 
this morning, despite 1500 J/kg of analyzed SBCAPE. To the 
northeast, thunderstorms have begun to fire in eastern Quebec where 
the instability gradient is maximized. This is further evident on 
the visible satellite where the most agitated cumulus are focused 
over the Northeast Kingdom, with lesser vertical motion evident 
across northern New York. Closer to home here, GOES-19 satellite 
depicts some dry air aloft in the 500-300mb layer with little 
improvement depicted upstream. Models have picked up this weaker 
shower trend quite nicely in the HRRR. Showers will mainly be 
focused over the Northeast Kingdom through this afternoon, with 
better chances closer toward 8 PM. the Storm Prediction Center has 
placed the NEK in a Marginal Risk for Severe Storms (level 1 out of 
5) for this afternoon and evening. Some small hail to half an inch 
and briefly gusty winds up to 40 MPH may be possible under any 
stronger storms. Though the confidence in any widespread storms is 
low. Elsewhere an isolated terrain driven shower may be possible, in 
addition to a few isolated showers along the western lake breeze of 
Lake Champlain. Most locations today look to remain on the dry side. 
An isolated rumble of thunder in the Champlain Valley or higher 
terrain cannot be ruled out with decent instability in place, should 
a shower grow tall enough to break through the subsidence inversion. 
Shower chances will once again decrease after sunset with the loss 
of diurnal heating. 

Troughing will slide east with surface high pressure building in by 
Friday. More calm and quieter conditions are expected through 
Saturday. Temperatures will be relatively seasonable in the mid to 
upper 70s. A radiational cooling night is increasingly likely Friday 
night with lows potentially dipping to the upper 40s to low to mid 
50s. A few pocket low 40s may be possible in the decoupled protected 
valleys of the Adirondacks and eastern Greens. Saturday looks to be 
the best of the weekend with temperatures in the low to mid 70s, and 
mountain temperatures in the low to mid 60s. It will be a great day 
for outdoor activities with plenty of sun and little in the way of 
wind. Shower chances return by Sunday as weak northern and southern 
stream energies interact over the North Country. There is still some 
questions lingering on how much of an interaction there will be, 
with some model solutions depicting the southern stream breaking 
down and remaining south for a potentially drier Sunday. There does 
look to be a weak cold front associated with the northern stream of 
energy that has better confidence in at least some shower activity 
by Sunday night.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Large scale troughing will dominate next week, leading 
to seasonable temperatures and a few shower chances. Humidity will 
also be on the lower side, with dew points generally in the 50s and 
low 60s. After any lingering showers exit Monday, the next chance of 
rain does not look to be until late Wednesday from a cold front, and 
then over the weekend from another potential low pressure system. 
Highs look to be in the 70s and low 80s, and lows look to be in the 
50s in most places. The coldest areas should see some temperatures 
in the 40s and the warmest places, notably along Lake Champlain, 
should see some lows in the 60s. Overall, it looks to be a pleasant 
and relatively uneventful stretch of summer weather.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...Isolated showers will move through northern
Vermont today, and one could briefly pass through EFK. A drop to
MVFR or IFR visibility would be likely, with thunder possible.
Elsewhere should be dry and VFR, though a brief light shower cannot
be completely ruled out. The shower activity ends in the evening.
Patchy fog will form tonight. It is expected at MPV and SLK, and
likely at EFK and MSS (~60 percent chance). Fog is not expected but
cannot be ruled out elsewhere. The fog should lift by around 13Z and
VFR conditions will prevail for the rest of the day. Winds should be
generally northwesterly and around and under 10 KT today, going
light or terrain driven overnight, before returning northwesterly
Friday.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Likely SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Monday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
